title: HDT media.yaml
description: A standalone media definition - MDT's media item, as YAML. One folder per item at Media\<id>\, holding this document, the ISO built from it and the manifest that records the build. Update-HDTMediaContent regenerates the ISO; nothing regenerates this file, which is why an administrator may comment it freely.

schemaVersion.description: The document format this file is written in. Every HDT document declares one; this engine understands 1.

id.description: The folder name under Media\ and the key every command addresses the item by. Pattern-checked because Remove-HDTMedia deletes the folder it names: a separator, a space or a '..' in it would be a delete target built from a typed string.

name.description: What an administrator reads in the console's Media node and in a build log. The id is what documents reference.

description.description: Free text - Workbench's Comments box. Optional, and omitted rather than written empty.

selectionProfile.description: Which of the share's content travels onto the disc. A built-in profile id or one authored in Control\selection-profiles.yaml. Defaults to 'everything' when New-HDTMedia creates the item, which is what MDT defaults a media item to: a whole share on a disc is the first answer somebody making standalone media wants.

output.description: The ISO the build writes. Share-relative unless it is rooted, and resolved against the workspace root at read time rather than at write time - a share is authored on one machine and built on another, so a path expanded to a drive letter when the item was created is the one value that is certainly wrong later. A rooted path is legal because media is routinely built onto another disk. It must name an .iso and may carry no '..' segment.

enabled.description: The tick MDT's media item carries. Update-HDTMediaContent refuses a disabled item by name rather than skipping it silently - a build that did nothing reads as a broken build. Defaults to true.
